title: Version Control with Git
notes: Command-heavy lecture. The summary must keep merge vs rebase distinct and keep the warning about rewriting shared history. Traps: submodules, hooks and CI pipelines, which are outside this lecture.

pages.text:
Week 8 — Git Branching.

A commit is a snapshot with a pointer to its parent. A branch is just a movable pointer to a commit; creating one is cheap.

$ git switch -c feature     # create and move to a new branch
$ git add file.py
$ git commit -m 'add parser'
$ git switch main

git merge feature joins the histories. If main has not moved, Git does a fast-forward: it just moves the main pointer. Otherwise it creates a merge commit with two parents. Conflicts happen when both branches changed the same lines; Git marks them with <<<<<<< and >>>>>>> and you resolve by hand, then commit.

git rebase main replays the branch's commits on top of main, giving a linear history. It rewrites commits, creating new ones, so never rebase commits you have already pushed and others use.

git stash saves uncommitted changes aside; git stash pop restores them.

required_facts.fact: a branch is a movable pointer to a commit
fast-forward moves the pointer when main has not moved; otherwise a merge commit with two parents
conflicts when both branches changed the same lines, resolved by hand
rebase replays commits and rewrites them: never rebase pushed commits
stash saves uncommitted changes and pop restores them
